 Nets Notes: Randle, Porter, C. Johnson, Fernandez, Brown
 By Arthur Hill |
 at October 31, 2026 9:51 pm 
 The Nets need a heavy dose of veteran leadership from Julius Randle and Michael Porter Jr. to recover from their 0-5 start, writes Brian Lewis of The New York Post . After going to overtime at Boston on Tuesday, the team fell flat in Friday’s NBA Cup opener, losing at home by 16 points to Detroit. Lewis states that the players’ bad body language offers a warning that the downward spiral could continue.
 “[We’ve] just got to be mentally tougher, understand what’s going on in the game, understand what we’re trying to accomplish, what we can take advantage of, stuff like that,” Randle said. “But we just have to have better recognition in-game of what’s going on and just be better from there. But we get adversity right now as a group, and it just deflates us as a team. So I have to find a way to keep the group together, and get us out of those ruts when we’re facing those types of situations.”  
 Adversity has been a common theme for the Nets, who are the only winless team left in the East. While Randle and Porter are looked at as team leaders, Lewis notes that their future in Brooklyn may be short. Porter has a $40.8MM expiring contract and could be moved by the trade deadline, while Randle holds a $35.8MM player option for next summer and might decide to test free agency.
 Despite their situations, coach Jordi Fernandez has been happy with the effort they’ve made to provide stability on an otherwise young roster.
 “I always want them to lead and it’s got to come out of an honest place. I cannot force them to be out of character,” Fernandez said. “I think they’re both good people and they both mean well, so whatever they’re comfortable doing I’m very happy they’re trying their best to help the group. And they’ve done it from the beginning, so I’m not concerned about that.” 
 There’s more on the Nets:
 Chaney Johnson made his second career start on Friday, replacing Egor Demin , who is sidelined with a right leg bone bruise, Lewis adds in a separate story . The 6’7″ forward was used in the backcourt to match up with Cade Cunningham and finished with six points, a steal and a block in nearly 19 minutes. “I thought Chaney’s effort and purpose and everything he’s done so far, it’s been very good. I think he’s taking advantage of his minutes,” Fernandez said. “We just need everybody to have the same intentions and intensity and play as hard as he plays. And I think then we will be OK.” 
 Fernandez took responsibility for the team’s fragile mental state after Friday’s loss, C.J. Holmes of The New York Daily News relays in a subscriber-only story. Brooklyn seized an early 10-point lead, but wasn’t able to respond when Detroit began to pull away. “When we hit adversity, it’s about how we react,” Fernandez said. “You see dropped shoulders and not the same energy. We can control those things. … There’s a lot of the team not coming together. The team is going separate ways. I’m responsible for that.” 
 Rookie guard Mikel Brown Jr. , who played 23 minutes on Friday, will be held out of Sunday’s game at Indiana for back management, according to Lewis ( Twitter link ).
